Visualize the named entities of parsed documents

Source: R/entity_visualize.R
entity_visualize.Rd

Shows documents parsed by spacy_parse() with their named entities highlighted and labelled, as HTML made by displaCy, spaCy's visualizer (see https://spacy.io/usage/visualizers#ent).

Usage

entity_visualize(x, entities = NULL, colors = NULL, view = FALSE)

Arguments

x

the output of spacy_parse(), best with offsets = TRUE (see Details), or of entity_consolidate()

entities

the entity labels to highlight, as a character vector such as c("PERSON", "ORG"). The default, NULL, highlights the entities of every label, and character(0) highlights none. The labels are those of the language model (see its "Label scheme" on https://spacy.io/models) and of any entity rules, and are matched regardless of case.

colors

a named character vector of colours for labels, such as c(ORG = "#7aecec", PERSON = "lightblue"), whose names are labels and whose values are colours in any form that CSS has. displaCy has colours of its own for the labels of spaCy's models, and shows other labels in grey.

view

logical; if TRUE, also open the result in the browser, or in the viewer that the browser option is set to (see utils::browseURL()).

Value

a character vector of length one, with the HTML for all the documents. It is a fragment and not a whole page, so that it can be put into a page, an R Markdown document or a Shiny app. It is returned invisibly when view = TRUE, and is "" when there are no documents.

Details

The entities are those of the entity column of the parse, so it needs entity = TRUE, the default of spacy_parse(). They include any from rules given to spacy_initialize() as entity_patterns. The documents are not processed again.

A parse does not keep the texts, so the text shown is made from the tokens. With spacy_parse(x, offsets = TRUE) the tokens are spaced as they were in the text. Otherwise there is a space between every two tokens, also before punctuation and within words that spaCy splits, such as did n't; the entities are the same, and a message, given once in a session, says how to get the spacing of the text. In the output of entity_consolidate() each entity is one token, shown with the concatenator that joined its parts.

The documents are shown in the order of the parse, each in a block of its own. A document without entities, or without any of the labels in entities, is shown as plain text. The HTML is made by spaCy, which is initialized if it has not been.

See also

spacy_parse(); entity_extract() and spacy_extract_entity() for the entities as data.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
spacy_initialize()

txt <- head(data_char_sentences, 8)
parsed <- spacy_parse(txt, offsets = TRUE)

# save as HTML
html <- entity_visualize(parsed)

# open in the browser
entity_visualize(parsed, view = TRUE)

# only some labels, and a colour of one's own
entity_visualize(parsed, entities = c("ORG", "GPE"), colors = c(GPE = "gold"),
                 view = TRUE)
} # }
